reviews.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended Closing a gzip/deflate dataset can race with an active read because the decompressor is closed before the HTTP body without synchronizing with the read.
1 open issue - [Synchronize decompressor cleanup with active reads](https://github.com/Azure/azure-kusto-go/pull/364#discussion_r4548668089) · New
What changed in this PR Addresses #359 by making iterative query dataset closure close the underlying response reader, so stalled reads can be interrupted without cancelling the original request. **Changes:** - Retains the frame reader and closes it from `IterativeDataset.Close()`. - Uses `sync.Once` to prevent repeated underlying close calls. - Adds a regression test for stalled-read interruption and single-close behavior. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `azkustodata/​query/​v2/​iterative_dataset.go` | Connects dataset closure to response-reader cleanup. | | `azkustodata/​query/​v2/​iterative_dataset_close_test.go` | Tests stalled reads and repeated closure. | | `azkustodata/​query/​v2/​frame_reader.go` | Makes reader closure idempotent and preserves its error. |
Review effort: Balanced

### 🟡 Changes recommended The shutdown path relies on undocumented concurrent Read/Close guarantees, risking races or blocked compressed reads, and can incorrectly report shutdown-induced read errors as failures.
2 open issues - [Document or support concurrent read interruption on Close](https://github.com/Azure/azure-kusto-go/pull/364#discussion_r4585691236) · New - [Avoid reporting shutdown-induced compressed read errors](https://github.com/Azure/azure-kusto-go/pull/364#discussion_r4585691281) · New
1 resolved since last review - [Synchronize decompressor cleanup with active reads](https://github.com/Azure/azure-kusto-go/pull/364#discussion_r4548668089)
Review effort: Max

### 🟡 Changes recommended The promoted ToDataset() bypasses request-context cancellation, potentially leaving stalled HTTP reads alive, while the new test does not reliably verify stalled-read cleanup.
2 open issues - [Override ToDataset to cancel the request context on close](https://github.com/Azure/azure-kusto-go/pull/364#discussion_r4597860048) · New - [Verify the stalled read and body cleanup with a tracking response body](https://github.com/Azure/azure-kusto-go/pull/364#discussion_r4597860119) · New
2 resolved since last review - [Document or support concurrent read interruption on Close](https://github.com/Azure/azure-kusto-go/pull/364#discussion_r4585691236) - [Avoid reporting shutdown-induced compressed read errors](https://github.com/Azure/azure-kusto-go/pull/364#discussion_r4585691281)
Review effort: Max

### 🟡 Changes recommended The stalled-response tests explicitly close the dataset, leaving automatic request cancellation and response-body cleanup after a decoding error without regression coverage.
1 open issue - [Test cancellation when ToDataset exits early on a stalled malformed stream](https://github.com/Azure/azure-kusto-go/pull/364#discussion_r4599636448) · New
2 resolved since last review - [Verify the stalled read and body cleanup with a tracking response body](https://github.com/Azure/azure-kusto-go/pull/364#discussion_r4597860119) - [Override ToDataset to cancel the request context on close](https://github.com/Azure/azure-kusto-go/pull/364#discussion_r4597860048)
Review effort: Max

### 🟡 Changes recommended Tests do not verify request-context cancellation or cancellation-safe decompressor shutdown ordering, and reader ownership on constructor errors remains undocumented.
4 open issues - [Test read, decompressor, and body cleanup ordering](https://github.com/Azure/azure-kusto-go/pull/364#discussion_r4627464408) · New - [Assert materialization cancels the outbound request context](https://github.com/Azure/azure-kusto-go/pull/364#discussion_r4627464502) · New - [Test cancellation when ToDataset exits early on a stalled malformed stream](https://github.com/Azure/azure-kusto-go/pull/364#discussion_r4599636448) - [Document reader ownership when construction fails](https://github.com/Azure/azure-kusto-go/pull/364#discussion_r4627464565) · New

review_comments.body: Closing a gzip/deflate dataset while `advance()` is reading can race inside the decompressor: `response.originalCloser.Close()` closes it before the HTTP body. `sync.Once` only serializes close calls, not reads. Make the wrapper close the HTTP body first, synchronize decompressor cleanup with completion of the active read, and add compressed-response race coverage.

When `Close` overlaps a pending read, this assumes the caller-supplied `io.ReadCloser` supports concurrent `Read`/`Close` and that closing it interrupts the read. The public constructor documents neither requirement, and a raw `*gzip.Reader` can race without unblocking its underlying stream. Provide a transport-level interruption path, or explicitly document the stronger reader contract on `NewIterativeDataset`.

When this interrupts a stalled gzip/deflate read, `originalCloser.Close` returns the induced read error, so an otherwise successful dataset shutdown now reports failure. Keep closing the reader while preserving the previous nil result (or filtering shutdown-induced errors), and add a compressed dataset test that checks the return value.

@pcbeingused333 - Could we instead create a cancellable request context before starting the HTTP query and have  dataset.Close() cancel it? The reader goroutine could then exit the interrupted read and perform decompressor/body cleanup sequentially. This would avoid concurrent decompressor read/close and avoid returning the shutdown-induced read error through Close() . 

We should document that  Close()  initiates cancellation rather than waiting for cleanup, and add gzip/deflate stalled-read regression tests.

Could we document that callers supplying a reader to  NewIterativeDataset are responsible for interrupting blocked reads, rather than closing that reader concurrently from dataset.Close() ? The reader goroutine can retain its existing cleanup responsibility after reading stops. 

For  client.IterativeQuery , the SDK owns the HTTP request and can interrupt it through request-context cancellation.

The promoted `ToDataset()` runs on the inner dataset, so its deferred `Close()` never calls `reqCancel`. Consequently, `Client.Query` never cancels the new request context, and an early materialization error can leave a stalled HTTP read alive. Override `ToDataset()` and defer the wrapper's `Close()` before delegating so every conversion releases the request context.

Receiving a table and sleeping does not prove that the next body read has begun, so the test can pass without exercising a stalled read. The checks at lines 91–99 also do not prove reader cleanup: `Tables()` closes independently, and request cancellation can disconnect the server before body cleanup. Use a tracking response body to signal the read after the prefix and `Close()`, and wait for those signals before and after `ds.Close()`.
@pcbeingused333 - I guess we would need to accommodate this.

The stronger test would establish this sequence:

Reader reaches the stalled read
    ↓
Test calls dataset.Close()
    ↓
Blocked read exits
    ↓
SDK closes the response body

The new stalled-response tests only call `ds.Close()` explicitly, so they would still pass if this override were removed and `ToDataset()` reverted to the promoted method. That would leave the request alive when materialization exits early on a decoding error. Please add a regression test that calls `ToDataset()` or `Client.Query` on a malformed stream that subsequently stalls, then verifies request cancellation and response-body cleanup without explicitly closing the dataset.

Couple of comments @pcbeingused333 

1. Could we also close res when NewIterativeDataset fails? No reader goroutine is started on that path, so nothing subsequently closes the translated response reader. reqCancel() cancels the request but does not invoke that reader’s Close()

2. Could we add tests for this override on both successful conversion and an early conversion error while the remaining response is stalled? Removing this override currently leaves the root-package tests passing. Please verify request cancellation and exactly-once body cleanup through both IterativeQuery().ToDataset() and Client.Query(). A multi-table/multi-fragment success case should also ensure cancellation does not happen prematurely.

3. The current assertions observe the HTTP body, not the decompressor. Skipping decompressor Close() still leaves these tests passing. Could we instrument the actual gzip reader and assert: HTTP read returns → gzip read returns → gzip close completes → HTTP body closes? Please cover payload and trailer stalls, exactly-once cleanup, and a decompressor cleanup error that must not prevent HTTP-body closure. Equivalent deflate coverage would be useful.

The order tests finish `ReadAll` before closing the reader, while the client tests observe only the HTTP body. Neither verifies that dataset cancellation lets the decompressor's `Read` return before its `Close` begins. Add an instrumented gzip/deflate dataset test for payload and trailer stalls that checks read completion, decompressor close completion, then HTTP-body close.

These success assertions only observe body cleanup, which `readRoutine` already performs at EOF even if `cancelOnCloseDataset.ToDataset` never calls `reqCancel`. Thus the success case does not verify that materialization releases the request context. Please capture the outbound request's context in `trackingTransport` and assert that its `Done()` channel closes after `call(t, client)` for both call paths. Checking the returned dataset's context would not suffice, since the inner dataset cancels that independently.

The dataset takes ownership of `r` only after successful construction: if `newFrameReader` fails, this function returns without closing it. Please document that callers must close `r` on constructor errors, so callers following this ownership contract do not leak the response body.

@pcbeingused333 
Add an integrated test that closes an actual iterative dataset while its decompressor is blocked reading HTTP data.

The test should:

1. Serve a compressed V2 response from a local HTTP server, then stall it.
2. Instrument the real gzip/deflate reader to record when Read() returns and when Close() starts/completes.
3. Confirm a decompressor read is genuinely blocked—use synchronization, not just a sleep.
4. Call dataset.Close() before the stalled read finishes.
5. Assert:
HTTP Read returns
→ decompressor Read returns
→ decompressor Close starts and completes
→ HTTP body Close starts
Also verify exactly-once closure and that the reader goroutine terminates.

Cover gzip payload stalls, gzip trailer stalls, and deflate payload stalls. Include a decompressor-close error case proving the HTTP body still closes.

The key difference from existing tests: cancellation must trigger the cleanup sequence, rather than calling Close() only after ReadAll() has already finished. Run the test under -race where supported

@pcbeingused333 
The current assertions verify response-body cleanup, but EOF triggers that cleanup even without request-context cancellation. We should capture the outbound request’s context in trackingTransport and assert its Done() channel is closed after both IterativeQuery().ToDataset() and Client.Query() return successfully.

comments.body:
Addressed the compressed-response cleanup concern: the transport closes first, active reads finish before decompressor cleanup, and repeated closes share the same result. Added gzip/deflate stalled-read coverage and a close-order regression test; both affected packages pass under the race detector.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

Thanks @pragatibaheti. Reworked along the lines you suggested:

- `Client.IterativeQuery` now creates a cancellable request context and cancels it from `dataset.Close()`, which interrupts a read blocked on the response body.
- `iterativeDataset.Close()` no longer closes the reader; it cancels the dataset context and returns nil. The reader goroutine keeps its cleanup responsibility and closes the decompressor/body sequentially after the read stops, so there is no concurrent decompressor read/close and no shutdown-induced error is returned from `Close()`.
- Documented on `NewIterativeDataset` that the dataset closes the reader from its read goroutine, `Close()` only initiates cancellation (it does not wait for cleanup), and callers supplying their own reader are responsible for interrupting blocked reads.
- The concurrency changes in `response.go`/`frame_reader.go` are reverted as no longer needed. The test now checks that `Close()` does not close the reader mid-read and that cleanup happens exactly once after the read is interrupted.

I also added stalled-read regression tests for identity, gzip and deflate responses (`azkustodata/kusto_close_stalled_test.go`): an `httptest` server sends the dataset header and the primary table header and then stalls; `Client.IterativeQuery` -> `Close()` returns nil, the dataset's `Tables()` channel closes and the server sees the connection released within 2s, under `-race`.

`go test -race ./azkustodata/query/v2 ./azkustodata/internal/response` and the new test pass.

This comment was prepared with the help of an AI coding assistant (Claude Code).

Thanks @pragatibaheti, both points addressed:

- `cancelOnCloseDataset` now overrides `ToDataset()` and defers its own `Close()`, so `Client.Query` releases the request context on every exit path, including early materialization errors.
- The stalled-read test now wraps the response body via a custom `http.Client` transport. It waits until a body `Read` is in flight and stays blocked, calls `ds.Close()`, then waits for the SDK to close the body, and asserts the body was not closed while a read was still in flight.

`go test -race -count=3 -run TestIterativeQueryCloseStalled ./azkustodata/` and `./azkustodata/query/...` pass. (`TestSchemas/TestNoAuthHttps` needs DNS and fails in a sandbox without network; unrelated.)

This comment was prepared with the help of an AI coding assistant (Claude Code).

Thanks @pragatibaheti, pushed a follow-up commit:

- `Client.IterativeQuery` now closes the response reader when `NewIterativeDataset` fails (no read goroutine exists on that path, so nothing else would), in addition to cancelling the request context.
- Added root-package tests (`kusto_todataset_test.go`) for `cancelOnCloseDataset.ToDataset()` through both `IterativeQuery().ToDataset()` and `Client.Query()`: a multi-table success case (both primary tables arrive complete, body closed exactly once, never mid-read) and an early conversion error with a stalled remaining response (request cancellation reaches the server, body closed exactly once, without an explicit `Close()`), plus a test that the body is closed when dataset creation fails on a non-JSON response. Removing the `ToDataset` override or the new `res.Close()` makes these fail.
- On point 3: you were right that the previous wording did not hold: `gzip.Reader.Close` does not close the underlying body, so it cannot be "covered by its observable effect". `response.go` now builds the decompressors through package-level `newGzipReader` / `newFlateReader` variables (same behavior), and `response_order_test.go` wraps the real `compress/gzip` and `compress/flate` readers with spies. It asserts the order HTTP read -> decompressor read -> decompressor close -> body close for gzip and deflate, with a stalled payload and a gzip stalled-then-truncated trailer, exactly one close of each, and that an error from the decompressor's `Close` is returned but still closes the body. Removing `o.ReadCloser.Close()` from `originalCloser.Close` now fails these tests. These lock in existing behavior rather than fix a new bug.
- The new commits sit on top of your `master` merge (no force-push).

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

Thanks @pragatibaheti. The three points from the latest review are on the branch:

- `trackingTransport` stores the outbound query request's context. `TestToDatasetReleasesRequest` asserts that context's `Done` channel is closed after both `IterativeQuery().ToDataset()` and `Client.Query()` return on the success path. Body cleanup at EOF does not satisfy that assertion.
- `NewIterativeDataset` documents that ownership of the reader transfers only when construction succeeds. If construction fails, the caller still closes the reader.
- `TestIterativeQueryCloseOrderCompressed` serves a compressed V2 response and stalls it, with the real gzip or deflate reader wrapped so the test can see when `Read` returns and when `Close` starts and finishes. It waits until a decompressor `Read` is blocked inside an HTTP `Read` (in-flight counters held for 100ms, not a sleep), then calls `dataset.Close()`. The recorded order is: the stalled HTTP read returns, the decompressor read returns, decompressor `Close` starts and completes, then the HTTP body `Close` starts. Each close happens once and the dataset's read goroutine finishes. Subtests cover a gzip payload stall, a gzip trailer stall, a deflate payload stall, and a decompressor `Close` error for gzip and deflate; the body still closes in the error case. The package tests run under the race detector.

This comment was prepared with the assistance of an AI coding assistant.
@pcbeingused333 - Please add an entry in CHANGELOG.md and we should be good to go

@pragatibaheti added the CHANGELOG.md entry under Unreleased > Fixed.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
